cover letter
Bachelor's degree in business administration, construction management, engineering; possession of an engineer's license, contractor's license, journey level status in a trade
Must have served a four-year apprenticeship and/or equivalent combination of skill/work experience
Must have been employed as a journey-level plumber/pipefitter for a minimum of 4 years.

The Plumber Pipefitter installs or repairs water, gas, waste, and other types of piping and pipe fittings, valves, fixtures, and related plumbing equipment. This position outlines work and measures to locate pipe positions from drawings or other written specifications. The Plumber Pipefitter cuts, threads, bends, assembles, and fastens pipe; makes computations relating to pressure, flow, and required pipe size; and tests to determine whether finished pipe meets specifications, to keep plumbing systems in good working order.
Installation, alteration, maintenance, and repair of plumbing systems, fittings, and fixtures in on-campus and RSSP buildings and facilities.
Understanding and planning the methods and procedures required to complete installation and repair work on piping systems, including underground and in high-rise buildings.
Prepares detailed isometric drawings, showing measurements and materials, using information obtained from blueprints and verbal instructions.
Fabricates a wide variety of campus piping systems and related components.

Installs and repairs Campus plumbing systems, including but not limited to: gas lines, domestic water heating systems, sewer systems, vent systems, acid-waste systems, water lines, backflow prevention systems, and other components.
Demonstrates the ability to join similar and dissimilar metals using the proper methods, techniques, and materials.

Demonstrates at all times, good communication skills with management, campus community, including students, building managers, academic personnel, and craft personnel, in a multi-cultural environment.
Execute all job assignments in a timely manner.
Works from drawings or prepares detailed project drawings showing measurements, materials, and other required information, using building blueprints, verbal instructions, and other sources.
Perform planned and emergency maintenance, inspections, test operations, troubleshooting, and documentation of work performed.
Must be available to respond to emergencies, work on-call, rotating swing shift, and holidays.
Work is subject to inspection while in progress and upon completion.
As required, handles hazardous waste and is responsible for safely handling, properly containing and labeling, and following appropriate emergency procedures related to hazardous waste materials.

Performs all work while conforming with EH&S health and safety policies, OSHA and other applicable federal, state and local fire, health, safety, emergency-preparedness, pollution-prevention policies, RSSP policies and procedures and University of Californias policies and procedures, including Code of Conduct, IIPP (Safety and Health Procedures), Hazardous Materials Communications Program, Health and Safety Manual, as well as any other document authorized by the RSSP management to have bearing on employee safety and conduct.
Performs other duties as assigned.

General pipe fitting; utilizing all hand tools, including brazing, copper, soldering copper fittings, and connecting pipes with threaded, caulked, soldered, brazed, fused, and cemented joints, and hand tools.
Follow specifications on isometric drawings to fabricate and install piping.
Perform residential service calls, including faucets, tub and shower valves, water heaters, drain repairs, and sump pumps.
Applied knowledge of system operations.
Must have a thorough knowledge of local, state, and plumbing codes and plumbing standards.
Must have the ability to read and interpret blueprints and drawings
